content.content: A draft's record shall be `open` for as long as its draft has not landed and `landed` from that landing onward, and a `landed` record shall be kept and never returned to `open`.
content.rationale:
This node adds no state, no transition and no storage rule of its own; it is the requirement-shaped statement of the lifetime the prerequisite fixes, so each clause is a reading of one part of that prerequisite rather than a new commitment.

The `open` clause takes the prerequisite's definition of that value and turns it into a condition on the record's state: the clause is bounded by the draft's not having landed, not by a time, an act of opening or a stage. That keeps the requirement from deciding when a draft begins, which the prerequisite leaves to the draft model it rests on.

The `landed` clause takes the same definition from the other side and bounds it by the landing alone, because the prerequisite gives the landing as the single transition and gives that transition one content — recording the draft's edits into its node's change. One condition and no second transition: that is why the sentence carries no further trigger. Who performs a landing, and by what call, is deliberately unmentioned; naming it here would settle a surface the prerequisite defers.

The retention clause is the prerequisite's account of the landed end read as an obligation on the record's life rather than as a storage mechanism: the record is what a later reversal looks the draft up by, so a record dropped at landing would leave the files restored and no draft to name. Where the registry lives and how an entry is keyed are cited from before this requirement, not re-decided here.

The no-return clause follows from the values themselves as the prerequisite draws them, not from a rule added beside it: a `landed` record has nowhere to go, and a later draft arrives as its own record rather than by reopening this one. The clause is stated because a reader given only the forward transition stays free to reverse it.

Absent on purpose: any cap on open records, any barrier over them, any verb or output that would report a state, and any rule about when or by what call a draft is opened. Each belongs to a commitment the prerequisite puts elsewhere, and the requirement is complete without them: it fixes only which values one record takes, which way it moves, and that it stays where it ends.
